groups.title: Password Security
groups.question: Explain how you would store user passwords safely in your API, and why each step matters.

followUps.bcrypt & Adaptive Hashing: Why is a fast hash like SHA-256 a bad choice for passwords, and what does bcrypt's cost factor do?
followUps.Salt — Why Random Salts Matter: Two users pick the same password. What makes their stored hashes different, and what attack does that stop?

groups.title: JWT Authentication
groups.question: Walk through how JWT authentication works in an API, from login to a protected request, including how sessions end.

followUps.JWT Structure, Signing & the 'alg:none': Which part of a JWT actually provides security, and why should the server never trust the algorithm named in the token header?
followUps.Refresh Token Rotation & Token Revocatio: A refresh token gets stolen. How do rotation and a revocation list limit the damage?

groups.title: OAuth 2.0
groups.question: Explain how OAuth 2.0 lets one app access another service, and how you pick the right flow.

followUps.OAuth 2.0 Flows — Authorization Code vs: When would you use client credentials instead of the authorization code flow, and why is it unsafe in a browser app?
followUps.PKCE — Securing the Authorization Code F: A mobile app can't keep a client secret. What does PKCE add so an intercepted authorization code is useless?

groups.title: API Hardening
groups.question: Explain what you would configure to protect an API that a browser frontend calls, beyond authentication.

followUps.CORS — Cross-Origin Resource Sharing: What does CORS protect against, and what goes wrong if you allow any origin while also allowing credentials?
followUps.helmet.js & Security Headers: Name a security header that helmet.js sets and the attack it blocks.
